## Test-time compute and where gains come from

The appendix analyses behaviour in more depth.

- **Versus V3.** R1 and DeepSeek-V3 share the same base model. R1 gains most on STEM and reasoning (MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench, AIME), while V3 keeps an edge on IF-Eval.
- **Adaptive thinking length.** On a set of 2024 competition problems R1 uses under 7,000 thinking tokens on easier problems and over 18,000 on the hardest. GPT-4o averages 711 output tokens and solves far fewer.
- **Majority voting.** Voting over 64 samples lifts GPT-4o on AIME 2024 only from 9.3% to 13.4%, but lifts R1 from 79.8% to 86.7%. The authors argue independent samples cannot backtrack or build on each other, so non-reasoning models gain little. R1's pass@64 is 90.0%, showing its single chains sometimes fail.
- **Weak areas.** Math breakdown shows relative weakness in geometry and combinatorics.
- **Per stage.** On LiveCodeBench, gains at each stage come mainly from medium and hard problems.
